chunks.text: Body confidence is when someone accepts and behaves kindly towards their body.
That includes our size and shape, skin colour, appearance and any physical disabilities.
Jade Parnell from the Centre for Appearance Research says that having body confidence is about being accepting of your body and what it does for you.
If you feel positively about your body,
you are more likely to take part in activities and perform well in school.
However, a sense of body shame could make you step back, do less well at school and even feel down.
The cost of trying to achieve the perfect appearance is high and not worth the effort.
Nobody is ever perfect.
Even those who seem handsome or beautiful have things they hate about themselves.
Parnell says, "If you're always trying to look a certain way, you will have less time to make important memories."
It's important to realise that everybody is different, and we all belong to this society.
To develop a positive body image, Parnell says, "Try not to pay too much attention to the clothes you wear."
Of course you can express your personal fashion,
whether you prefer shirts and shorts,
or something more classic like a suit.
But you may also think about what your body does for you.
Do your legs make you run really fast?
Are you good at sports like volleyball?
She also suggests treating your body well by doing training, having fun,
going for a hike and getting plenty of sleep.
Remember that you are a lovely person no matter how you look.
